# Community support trial

## Rollout

The trial starts when the [announcement](./community-support-announcement.md)
is published in GitHub Discussions. Record its URL, publication date, and review
date (60 days later, Asia/Taipei) below. A published GitHub notice does not mean
the Discord notice or repository/site changes have been deployed.

- GitHub announcement: [#483](https://github.com/master-co/css/discussions/483), published and read back successfully.
- Trial start: 2026-11-04 (Asia/Taipei).
- Review date: 2027-01-03 (Asia/Taipei).
- GitHub pin: pending; use the discussion's **Pin discussion** menu.
- Discord notice: pending; an administrator should post the notice below and pin it in the existing support/announcement channels.
- Repository support routing: included in this change. Site navigation takes effect after the normal site deployment.

Keep the server and existing conversations. Redirect new technical questions to
Discussions. Do not bulk export chat messages or delete history. Rewrite only
still-valid, recurring technical answers into documentation after verification.

### Discord notice

Master CSS technical support is moving to GitHub Discussions for a 60-day trial:
https://github.com/master-co/css/discussions

Trial announcement: https://github.com/master-co/css/discussions/483

Ask in English or Chinese and include your version, framework, rendering mode,
and a small reproduction when relevant. Existing Discord conversations will
remain available. Maintainers will focus on asynchronous answers in Discussions;
real-time Discord support is not guaranteed. Please share feedback on the trial
in the [GitHub announcement](https://github.com/master-co/css/discussions/483).

歡迎使用中文或英文，並附上版本、框架、渲染模式與適用時的最小重現範例。

即時支援。試行意見請回覆 GitHub 公告。

## Weekly review

The maintainer can budget two 30-minute triage sessions per week; this is an
internal time budget, not a response-time commitment. At each review:

1. Check new Discussions, link duplicates, and ask for missing reproduction details.
2. Move reproducible defects to Issues or link the existing issue; avoid parallel support threads.
3. Mark resolved Q&A answers and identify verified answers worth adding to docs.
4. Record total support time across all channels, including Discord redirects and documentation work.

| Week ending (Asia/Taipei) | New support questions | Questions older than 7 days without an initial response | Repeat questions | Non-maintainer responders | Support minutes | Notes / thread links |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Count questions older than seven days as the unresolved inventory at review time,
not a sum across weeks. Count each non-maintainer responder once per week.
Leave measurements unfilled until collected; zero means an observed zero.
Record a pre-trial time estimate only if the maintainer can supply one and label
it as an estimate. Otherwise compare the first two trial weeks with the last two.

## Day-60 decision

Review maintenance time, unanswered questions, duplicate requests, reusable
answers, and participant feedback together. Report actual counts when volume is
small. Success means support is easier to handle and answers are easier to reuse;
message volume alone is not a success measure.

Keep Discussions as the primary support channel if it meets those goals. Retain
Discord chat only when a named volunteer can host it sustainably; otherwise keep
announcements and readable history. Announce any permission change before making
support channels read-only. Publish the review in the original GitHub discussion,
including any accessibility or participation problems raised by users.
